mainTopic: Whose view the משנה follows on vows of affliction, and a dispute about a vow that covers two loaves, only one of which causes real suffering
overview: The גמרא says that our משנה, and in fact the whole פרק, follows רבי יוסי, as רב הונא taught. It then explains what רבי יוסי means when he says a husband 'cannot nullify.' He cannot cancel these vows as עינוי נפש, but he can still cancel them as vows between him and her. Next comes a new case: a woman vowed off two loaves, and giving up one would cause her suffering but giving up the other would not. שמואל says that since the husband can cancel the vow for the first loaf, he can cancel it for both. רבי יוחנן says he can cancel it only for the loaf that causes suffering. A second version presents רבי יוחנן's ruling as his answer to a question from רב אסי. רב אסי then begins to challenge רבי יוחנן from a משנה about a woman who vowed to be a נזיר, and the challenge continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Our משנה follows רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the משנה follows רבי יוסי, backed by רב הונא's rule that the whole פרק follows רבי יוסי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Our משנה follows רבי יוסי, because רב הונא said that our whole chapter follows רבי יוסי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells us which תנא our משנה agrees with: רבי יוסי. It supports this with רב הונא's general rule about the whole פרק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי gives a narrower meaning to עינוי נפש (affliction) than the other חכמים. So when the משנה says a husband cannot cancel certain vows as affliction, it is following his narrower view. רב הונא's rule shows this is not a one-time claim; the whole פרק is built on רבי יוסי.

phrases.english: And our Mishnah is Rabbi Yosei's view.
As Rav Huna said:
Our entire chapter is Rabbi Yosei's view.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier discussion of whose view is followed about vows of affliction.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה, and the whole פרק, follows רבי יוסי.

steps.title: What does 'cannot nullify' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רבי יוסי means when he says the husband cannot nullify.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what does 'he cannot nullify' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a clarifying question about רבי יוסי's words. This sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Read literally, 'he cannot nullify' sounds like the husband has no power over these vows at all. The גמרא wants to know whether that is really what רבי יוסי means.

phrases.english: And what does 'he cannot nullify' mean?
phrases.notes: These words are quoted from רבי יוסי's statement in the משנה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Having said the משנה is רבי יוסי, the גמרא now clarifies his wording.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The exact scope of 'cannot nullify' in רבי יוסי's view.

steps.title: He cannot nullify as affliction, but can as between him and her
steps.stepSummary: The husband cannot cancel these vows as עינוי נפש, but he can cancel them as vows that affect him and her.
steps.simpleTranslation: It means he cannot nullify them because of affliction, but he can nullify them as vows between him and her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: 'cannot nullify' only means the husband cannot cancel these vows under the category of affliction. He still can cancel them under the other category, vows between him and her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A husband has two separate grounds for cancelling his wife's vows: עינוי נפש, and נדרים שבינו לבינה. רבי יוסי only removes these vows from the first group. The husband still has power over them through the second group.

keyTerms.meaning: Self-affliction, vows that cause the woman suffering
Vows that affect the relationship between husband and wife

steps.whatToRemember: For רבי יוסי, 'cannot nullify' is limited: not as affliction, but yes as vows between him and her.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't read 'cannot nullify' as 'the husband has no power at all.' He still can cancel, just under a different category.

phrases.english: He cannot nullify them as affliction,
but he can nullify them as vows between him and her.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשּׁוּם עִינּוּי נֶפֶשׁ אֲבָל מֵפֵר נְדָרִים שֶׁבֵּינוֹ לְבֵינָהּ
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He cannot nullify them as affliction, but he can as vows between him and her.

steps.title: שמואל: two loaves, nullify both
steps.stepSummary: שמואל rules that if a woman vowed off two loaves and only one causes suffering, the husband can cancel the vow for both.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: if she vowed off two loaves, and giving up one causes her suffering and giving up the other does not, then since he can nullify for the one that causes suffering, he can also nullify for the one that does not.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. שמואל rules about a single vow that covers two loaves, where only one of them causes real suffering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל's reasoning is מתוך: since the husband clearly has power over part of this vow, that power reaches the whole vow. So the vow is cancelled even for the loaf that would not cause suffering.

keyTerms.meaning: Since (because he can do one part, he can do the rest)

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
If she vowed off two loaves,
with one, she would suffer,
phrases.notes: Giving up this loaf, a good one, would cause her real suffering.

phrases.english: and with one, she would not suffer,
since he can nullify for the one that causes suffering,
he can nullify for the one that does not cause suffering.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל נָדְרָה מִשְׁתֵּי כִכָּרוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic about vows only partly involving affliction.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Since the husband can cancel for the loaf that causes suffering, he can cancel for both loaves.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: nullify only the loaf that causes suffering
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן disagrees: the husband can cancel only for the loaf that causes suffering.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב אסי said in the name of רבי יוחנן: he can nullify for the loaf that causes suffering, but not for the one that does not.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן takes the opposite position from שמואל in the same case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן does not accept the מתוך reasoning. He judges each loaf on its own, so the husband's power only reaches the part of the vow that actually causes suffering.

phrases.english: And Rav Asi said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
He can nullify for the one that causes suffering,
but he cannot nullify for the one that does not cause suffering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing view to שמואל's ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The husband can cancel the vow only for the loaf that causes suffering.

steps.title: Another version: רב אסי asks רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: In a second version, רב אסי asks רבי יוחנן what the law is in the two-loaves case.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say it went differently: רב אסי asked רבי יוחנן, 'If she vowed off two loaves, and with one she would suffer and with the other she would not, what is the law?'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second report of how רבי יוחנן's view came about. Here it starts as a question. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version, רבי יוחנן's ruling is an answer to a direct question rather than a statement on its own. The ruling itself stays the same; only the way it is reported changes.

phrases.english: And some say:

phrases.aramaic: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַב אַסִּי מֵרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rav Asi asked Rabbi Yochanan:
If she vowed off two loaves,
with one she would suffer and with one she would not,
what is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַב אַסִּי מֵרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second report of how רבי יוחנן's view came about.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the husband can nullify for both loaves or only for the one that causes suffering.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן answers: only the loaf that causes suffering
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers that the husband can cancel only for the loaf that causes suffering.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: he can nullify for the one that causes suffering, but not for the one that does not.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers רב אסי's question. His answer is the same ruling as in the first version.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both versions agree on רבי יוחנן's actual ruling. Each part of the vow is judged separately.
steps.whatToRemember: שמואל: the husband cancels for both loaves (מתוך). רבי יוחנן: he cancels only for the loaf that causes suffering.

phrases.english: He said to him:

phrases.aramaic: מֵפֵר לַמִּתְעַנָּה וְאֵין מֵפֵר לְשֶׁאֵין מִתְעַנָּה.
phrases.english: He can nullify for the one that causes suffering, but not for the one that does not.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ מֵפֵר לַמִּתְעַנָּה וְאֵין מֵפֵר לְשֶׁאֵין מִתְעַנָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב אסי's question in step 6.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Only the loaf that causes suffering can be nullified.

steps.title: רב אסי challenges from a woman who vowed to be a נזיר
steps.stepSummary: רב אסי begins a challenge against רבי יוחנן from a משנה about a woman who vowed נזירות, then drank wine and became טמא from the dead.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אסי raised an objection: a woman who vowed to be a נזיר, and she was drinking wine and becoming impure from the dead...
steps.whatsHappening: רב אסי starts quoting a משנה in order to challenge רבי יוחנן. The quote continues on the next amud, and the point of the challenge comes there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is a woman who vowed נזירות and then broke her vow. Her vow includes several different restrictions, so it can be tested against רבי יוחנן's idea that each part of a vow is judged on its own.

keyTerms.meaning: A person who vowed to avoid wine, cutting hair and טומאה from the dead
Becomes impure through contact with the dead

phrases.english: He raised an objection against him:
A woman who vowed to be a nazir,
phrases.notes: This is a משנה in נזיר (23a).

phrases.english: and she was drinking wine,
and becoming impure from the dead

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי יוחנן's ruling from steps 5 and 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's ruling that only the part of the vow that causes suffering can be nullified.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה about a woman's vow of נזירות will be used against רבי יוחנן's view; the details of the challenge continue after this point.
